title: Interpret request
description: What Unity POSTs to /interpret. This file is the canonical contract between the two repositories: the Unity project produces it, this backend consumes it, and the request validator in template.yaml is a copy of it trimmed to what API Gateway's draft-4 validator supports. Keep the three in step. Every value here is a FINISHED RESULT computed by the C# math engine - the backend performs no calculation of its own, which is what makes it safe to hand these numbers to a language model.

schemaVersion.description: Wire format version. Bumped only for a breaking shape change; a mismatch is logged by the backend rather than rejected, so an older Unity build keeps working.

equation.description: The surface as the student typed it, e.g. 'x^2 - y^2'. UNTRUSTED INPUT: it is user text that ends up inside a prompt, so the backend restricts it to the character set of the supported math grammar before use.

point.description: The clicked point in MATH coordinates, not Unity's. Unity's world X is x, world Z is y, and world Y is the height f.

gradient.description: First derivatives, estimated by central difference in SurfaceAnalyzer.

steepestAscentHeadingDegrees.description: Direction of steepest ascent, degrees anticlockwise from the +x axis. IGNORED by the backend when isCriticalPoint is true, because on level ground the gradient is numerical noise and its direction means nothing. Always present because Unity's JsonUtility cannot omit a field.

curvature.description: Second derivatives - the Hessian - estimated from a 3x3 stencil.

d2fdxdy.description: Mixed partial - the twist in the surface.

discriminant.description: d2fdx2 * d2fdy2 - d2fdxdy^2. The quantity the second-derivative test reads.

classification.description: The verdict the C# second-derivative test already reached. The backend echoes 'kind' straight back in its response and never derives a classification from the model's text.

kind.description: The finished label in words, e.g. 'saddle point' or 'sloping, curving upward in both directions'.

shape.description: Curvature alone, independent of whether the ground is level.

isCriticalPoint.description: Whether the gradient is effectively zero. This gates everything: the second-derivative test only identifies a maximum or minimum AT a critical point, so when this is false the point must not be described as one.

tangentPlane.description: Optional. The equation string TangentPlaneRenderer already formatted for display, passed along so the explanation and the on-screen label cannot disagree.

sampling.description: Optional. The numerical settings the derivatives were measured with. Not used to generate the explanation - it is here so a surprising answer can be traced back to the step size that produced it.
